name: Leona Navarro
life: “I still remember sharing an unfinished story with its first unknowing subject.” Sunday often includes a stop at the corner outside Coastal Barber, where Leona usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
voice: I would like the piece read once to the people in it before anybody publishes a line.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a soft blue checked shirt and a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. Leona has a wide brow and a narrow jaw, with a high puff tied with plain cord. Leona holds eye contact until the other person has finished during a conversation.
personality: Leona thinks best while walking. Sitting beneath someone's office clock makes Leona sound more certain than they feel, an effect close friends have learned to distrust.
agenda: To arrange a reading limited to the people represented.
family: Dolores Yeo is Leona’s cousin. Leona asks the question the rest of the family avoided. Dolores chooses an ordinary story to tell. They tend to get further with an important subject when it arrives in the middle of talk about dinner or work. Asked about *The split visit*, Dolores says, “I am paid for only one visit. I used the extra pair of hands to hang Dad's old framed diploma.”
connections: Elliot Cotton. The private reading gives someone portrayed in the book a place to raise concerns before publication.

reactions.situation: A relative wants the manuscript returned unopened
reactions.response: Leona returns the pages privately without treating keeping them closed as a verdict on the work.

reactions.situation: A street musician can't finish a familiar song
reactions.response: Leona starts a quiet conversation with the most impatient onlookers so the musician can recover their own time.

reactions.situation: When family demands an immediate answer
reactions.response: Leona asks them to walk to the corner together and listen until the corner comes.
